studies.title: Evaluation of betaine as a nutritional strategy to counteract cyclic heat stress in broilers: Performance, behavior, blood biochemistry, and tissue integrity.
studies.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the effects of betaine supplementation on performance, behavior, carcass characteristics, blood biochemistry, and immunohistochemistry of key organs under heat stress. One hundred twenty broiler chicks were randomly assigned to four groups (6 replicates of 5 chicks each) across two climate-controlled units. The groups included: G1, the control; G2, control with betaine; G3, heat-stressed; and G4, heat-stressed with betaine. All groups received a standard broiler diet, with 1 g/kg betaine added to groups 2 and 4. Heat stress negatively impacted performance, decreasing final body weight by 6.94% and weight gain by 7.25% in heat-stressed birds. Nonetheless, betaine supplementation notably increased final body weight (P < 0.05) in both normal and heat-stressed birds by 13.07% and 12.12%, respectively, and increased weight gain by 13.39% and 12.61%, respectively. Carcass characteristics were not affected by heat stress or betaine. Under heat stress (P < 0.05), behaviors such as feeding, foraging, walking, standing, and comfort decreased, while lying and drinking behaviors increased. Notably, betaine supplementation mitigated these shifts, restoring normal behavioral activity. Betaine enhanced physiological responses (P < 0.05), increasing serum levels of total protein (5.18%, 4.63%), albumin (2.06%, 1.445), total antioxidant capacity (13.41%, 11.46%), and superoxide dismutase (158.59%, 144.15%) in both normal and heat-stressed broilers. It also decreased total cholesterol, triglycerides, malondialdehyde, and inflammatory markers (P < 0.05). Histological and immunohistochemical analyses of the liver, intestine, and bursa revealed adverse effects of heat stress, but betaine supplementation partially alleviated the damage. Profitability improved with betaine in both environments, increasing net revenue and economic efficiency by 35% and 26% under normal conditions, and by 23% and 12% under heat stress, respectively. Betaine supplementation may mitigate the adverse effects of chronic cyclic heat stress in broilers by modulating immune and antioxidant defenses, reducing pro-inflammatory markers, and preserving intestinal tissue integrity.

studies.title: Betaine alleviates scleral remodeling in experimental myopia by regulating the TLR4/TAK1/NF-κB signaling pathway.
studies.abstract: Myopia progression is closely associated with scleral remodeling, in which oxidative stress, inflammation, and disruption of extracellular matrix (ECM) homeostasis may play important roles. Betaine has antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, but its effects on myopic scleral remodeling remain unclear. Public transcriptomic data, network pharmacology, and molecular docking were used as exploratory approaches to identify potentially relevant molecules and pathways. The in vivo and in vitro effects of betaine were subsequently evaluated in lens-induced myopia (LIM) guinea pigs and in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated primary guinea pig scleral fibroblasts, respectively. As a result, LIM induced axial elongation, a myopic refractive shift, scleral structural alterations, reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, inflammation, and disruption of ECM homeostasis. These changes were accompanied by activation of the toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/transforming growth factor-β-activated kinase 1 (TAK1)/nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) pathway and increased tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), and interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels. Betaine attenuated these changes, reduced matrix metalloproteinase-2 (MMP2) expression, and partially restored tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinases-2 (TIMP2), Collagen I, and α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) levels. In vitro, betaine partially restored cell viability, reduced ROS and inflammatory cytokine levels, suppressed TLR4/TAK1/NF-κB pathway activation, and ameliorated alterations in ECM-related proteins. Exploratory computational analyses suggested possible associations with inflammation-, oxidative stress-, and ECM-related pathways. Collectively, betaine attenuated LIM-induced myopia progression and scleral remodeling, potentially by reducing oxidative stress and inflammation, suppressing TLR4/TAK1/NF-κB signaling, and improving ECM homeostasis.

studies.title: Betaine Attenuates Hyperhomocysteinemia-Induced Cognitive Impairment by Suppressing Oxidative Stress and Activating the PI3K/AKT/GSK-3β Pathway.
studies.abstract: High homocysteine levels are a key risk factor for cognitive impairment, a major public health concern in aging societies. Although betaine is known to reduce Hcy levels, its effects on hyperhomocysteinemia (hHcy)-induced cognitive impairment and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we established an hHcy-induced cognitive impairment mouse model by feeding mice a high-methionine diet for 8 weeks, followed by betaine supplementation for 14 days. Betaine treatment attenuated hHcy-induced cognitive impairment. This improvement was accompanied by alleviation of neuropathological alterations and enhancement of antioxidant capacity. Notably, betaine suppressed reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, neuronal apoptosis, and Tau hyperphosphorylation at Ser396 and Thr231 in both mouse hippocampus and HT-22 cells. Mechanistically, betaine-induced activation of the PI3K/AKT/GSK-3β pathway was effectively blocked by the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. Notably, treatment with the ROS scavenger N-acetylcysteine (NAC) alone phenocopied this activation, suggesting that ROS functions as an upstream regulator of this signaling cascade. Collectively, our data demonstrate that betaine attenuates hHcy-induced cognitive impairment by suppressing oxidative stress-driven apoptosis and Tau pathology through modulation of the PI3K/AKT/GSK-3β signaling pathway. These findings suggest that betaine may hold promise for further preclinical and clinical studies, although long-term efficacy and safety evaluations remain necessary.

studies.title: Betaine Promotes Milk Protein Synthesis via Alleviating Oxidative Stress Caused by NEFA in Mammary Epithelial Cells of Dairy Cows.
studies.abstract:
Background

Fatty liver is highly prevalent in dairy cows and poses a significant challenge to the dairy industry by reducing both milk yield and quality, thereby inflicting substantial economic losses. Although dietary betaine supplementation has been demonstrated to enhance milk protein content, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain to be fully elucidated.

Objectives

This study aimed to elucidate the role of betaine in milk protein synthesis and the underlying mechanisms.

Methods

Blood, liver and mammary gland samples were obtained from healthy and fatty liver-affected bovines. The serum NEFA levels, oxidation and antioxidant enzyme systems and milk protein synthesis-related proteins expression were determined. In vitro, the bovine mammary epithelial cells (BMECs) were pretreated with 25 mM betaine/10 mM N-acetyl-L-cysteine (NAC) and then stimulated with NEFA.

Results

The results indicated an elevation in serum NEFA levels accompanied by enhanced oxidative stress (OS) and reduced protein levels related to milk protein synthesis (phosphorylated (p)-mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR)/mTOR, p-ribosomal protein S6 kinase 1 (S6K1)/S6K1, p-Janus kinase 2 (JAK2)/JAK2, p-signal transducer and activator of transcription 5 (STAT5)/STAT5 and β-casein) in dairy cows with fatty liver. In vitro, the results revealed betaine decreased the hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), malondialdehyde (MDA), and oxygen free radicals (OFR) contents, and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) activity in the supernatant, but increased the glutathione peroxidase (GPX), catalase (CAT), superoxide dismutase (SOD) and thioredoxin reductase (TrxR) activities; the reduced glutathione-to-oxidised glutathione (GSH/GSSG) ratio; and the total antioxidant capacity (T-AOC); and elevated protein levels related to milk protein synthesis in NEFA-treated BMECs.

Conclusions

These findings indicate that betaine reduces NEFA-induced OS and enhances milk protein synthesis, suggesting its potential as a nutritional intervention for enhancing milk protein content in dairy cows with metabolic disorders.

studies.title: Natural liquid betaine dietary supplementation improves growth performance, immuno-antioxidant responses, and stress resistance in Nile tilapia subjected to acu
studies.abstract: This work investigated the effects of natural liquid betaine (NATURA BETAINE) dietary supplementation on physiological performance and alleviation of acute ammonia toxicity in Nile tilapia. Four diets supplemented with 0.0, 0.8, 1.6, and 2.4 mL of liquid betaine /kg diet, representing the experimental treatments B0, B800, B1600, and B2400, respectively, in triplicates were used. Each replicate included 15 Nile tilapia fingerlings (N = 180, initial weight: 9.5 ± 0.429 g). Fish were fed at the rate of 4% of their body weight twice daily for 60 days. At the termination of this feeding trial, the groups B0 randomly divided into two parts B0 - ve and B0 + ve [control negative, and positive, respectively based on ammonia exposure. Then the groups B0 + ve, B800, B1600, and B2400 were subjected to acute ammonia challenge for 72 h, using ammonium chloride at 0.07 g/L. After the 60 days feeding trial, fish received liquid betaine supplemented diets displayed greater growth performance and feed utilization compared to the control group (B0). Additionally, betaine supplementation enhanced serum amylase and lipase concentrations and hematobiochemical metrics. The high dose of liquid betaine (B2400) increased antioxidant enzyme activities and lowered malondialdehyde concentration with increasing serum lysozyme activity and IgM concentrations, and phagocytic activity, and index. At molecular level, betaine dietary supplementation induced upregulations in the mRNA copies of some growth-, immuno- and antioxidant-related genes. Following ammonia exposure, betaine supplementation, particularly the highest dose (B2400) enhanced the cumulative survival rate and mitigated the inflammation signs and tissue degeneration caused by the ammonia challenge in liver, intestine, and gill tissues. In conclusion, dietary supplementation of NATURA BETAINE (at 2.4 mL kg<sup>-1</sup>) enhanced growth performance, optimized physio-biochemical homeostasis, reinforced innate immune and antioxidant responses which may enhance resilience to ammonia stress by improving survival and reducing tissue damage in Nile tilapia, supporting its application as an effective feed additive in aquaculture.

studies.title: Effects of Betaine on m6A Methylation, AMPK Signalling and Cytoplasmic Maturation in Porcine Oocytes.
studies.abstract: In vitro maturation (IVM) of oocytes is crucial in livestock breeding. Oocytes obtained by IVM are more susceptible to oxidative stress than in vivo, leading to low maturation rates. Betaine from red beetroot acts as an antioxidant and methyl donor, regulating epigenetic modifications in cell physiology. This study investigates Betaine's effects on porcine oocyte IVM, embryo development and underlying molecular mechanisms. Results demonstrate that 16 mmol/L Betaine significantly enhances the first polar body extrusion, cleavage and blastocyst rates compared to the control and other concentrations. Betaine elevates normal cortical granule distribution, normal spindle assembly, normal chromosome arrangement and overall m6A levels during IVM. It increases the antioxidant gene expression and mitochondrial function and decreases reactive oxygen species levels. However, Betaine's beneficial effects were diminished by AMPK inhibitor compound C. In conclusion, Betaine enhances porcine oocyte IVM and early embryo development by enhancing the antioxidant capacity and mitochondrial function pathway.

studies.title: Betaine inhibited adipogenesis in 3T3-L1 preadipocytes and alleviated obesity-related disorders in high-fat diet-fed C57BL/6 mice by modulating gut microbiota c
studies.abstract: The rising prevalence of obesity underscores the urgent need to develop safe and effective alternative therapies. Betaine, a quaternary amine-type alkaloid with established antioxidant and antiinflammatory properties, has shown promise in metabolic regulation. However, the mechanisms by which betaine exerts antiobesity effects, especially the contribution of gut microbiota and intestinal barrier function, remain to be elucidated. In this study, the effects of betaine on inhibiting adipogenesis in 3T3-L1 preadipocytes and alleviating obesity in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed C57BL/6 J mice were evaluated. The results revealed that betaine suppressed adipogenesis by downregulating adipogenic transcription factors and upregulating brown fat-specific markers. In HFD-fed mice, betaine treatment reduced body weight gain and tissue weight, improved glucose metabolism, alleviated inflammation, and mitigated tissue damage. Betaine also reshaped gut microbiota composition, enriching beneficial taxa (Muribaculaceae, Allobaculum, and Parabacteroides) and reducing harmful taxa (Colidextribacter and Desulfovibrionaceae), which correlated strongly with obesity-related indicators. Importantly, these beneficial effects were markedly attenuated in pseudo-germ-free mice, suggesting a relationship between gut microbiota and the antiobesity effects of betaine. It was hypothesized that betaine would alleviate obesity by suppressing adipogenesis and improving metabolic homeostasis through gut microbiota-dependent mechanisms, and the findings of this study supported this hypothesis. Overall, betaine exerts antiobesity effects through a gut microbiota-barrier-metabolism axis, combining inhibition of adipogenesis, promotion of browning, and restoration of intestinal barrier function. These findings provide novel mechanistic insights and suggest the potential of betaine as a dietary supplement or functional food for obesity and related metabolic disorders.

studies.title: Plant-derived betaine enhances barrier integrity and immune responses in canine intestinal epithelial cells and macrophages under endotoxin challenge.
studies.abstract: Interest in the utilization of novel plant-based extracts for supporting gut health and nutrition in companion animals is growing. The effect of betaine on canine intestinal barrier integrity and immune-related gene and protein expression by epithelial and macrophage-like cells was evaluated under conditions of inflammatory challenge from lipopolysaccharide (LPS). We evaluated: (1) the effect of betaine pre-treatment (0 to 1,000 µg/mL for 24 h) on the viability of canine intestinal epithelial MCA-B1 and macrophage-like DH82 cells; (2) epithelial barrier function of LPS-challenged MCA-B1 cells pre-treated with betaine, by measurement of 4-kDa fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC-dextran [FD4] flux); (3) gene and protein expression of tight junction proteins and adhesion molecules using quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) and proteomics; (4) anti- and pro-inflammatory and regulatory gene expression in LPS-challenged, betaine pre-treated, MCA-B1, DH82 and peripheral blood mononuclear cells and; (5) the phagocytic activity of DH82 cells pre-treated with betaine. No cytotoxicity of betaine against MCA-B1 or DH82 cells were observed. Betaine pre-treatment of MCA-B1 reduced FD4 permeability compared with untreated cells (P < 0.05), accompanied by increased (mRNA) expression of claudin-1 (P < 0.001) and E-cadherin (P < 0.05) and increased protein expression of junctional adhesion molecules (P < 0.05), vinculin (P < 0.05) and aquaporin-3 (AQP3; P < 0.01). Betaine pre-treatment of LPS-challenged cells also increased the expression of regulatory cytokines TGF-β1 (P < 0.01), TGF-β2 (P < 0.01), and IL-33 (P < 0.05) in MCA-B1 cells and reduced the expression of IL-6 (P < 0.05) and MyD88 (P < 0.01) in DH82 cells compared with untreated cells. In addition, betaine enhanced the phagocytic activity of DH82 cells (P < 0.01) compared with untreated cells. Confirmatory studies in vivo are needed but these results suggest that plant-derived betaine has potential as a nutritional supplement for companion animals to support gut health and immunity.

studies.title: Betaine Alleviates Favipiravir-induced Ovarian and Uterine Toxicity by Regulating Oxidative, Inflammatory, Cellular Death, Steroidogenic, Hormonal, and Histopat
studies.abstract: This study aims to evaluate the protective effects of betaine (BTN), an antioxidant agent, against ovarian and uterine toxicity caused by favipiravir (FVP), an antiviral agent, through multifaceted damage pathways. A total of 28 Wistar rats were divided into four experimental groups: Control, BTN (250 mg/kg), FVP (200 mg/kg), and FVP + BTN. At the end of the 10-day protocol, blood samples were collected along with ovarian and uterine tissue samples. Subsequently, the samples were subjected to biochemical analysis, qRT-PCR analysis, histological evaluation, and immunohistochemical studies. These methods assessed oxidative stress, inflammatory, apoptotic, and autophagic responses, hormonal changes, and overall tissue damage. FVP administration significantly increased oxidative stress (MDA, p < 0.001), inflammation (NF-κB, TNF-α, IL-1β, p < 0.001), apoptosis (Caspase-3, Bax, p < 0.001), and autophagy (Beclin-1, LC3A, p < 0.001); while decreasing antioxidant levels, Bcl-2, and steroidogenesis genes (CYP11A1, CYP17A1, CYP19A1, p < 0.001), and reducing serum AMH, E2, FSH, and LH values (p < 0.001). When BTN was administered concomitantly, most of these changes were reversed, antioxidant and hormonal balance were significantly restored, and the increases in oxidative, inflammatory, and apoptotic markers were reduced (p < 0.05-0.001). Histologically, betaine preserved tissue integrity by mitigating ovarian and uterine damage caused by FVP (p < 0.05). FVP caused multifaceted oxidative, inflammatory, apoptotic, and hormonal damage in ovarian and uterine tissues, while BTN significantly reduced these effects, preserving tissue integrity and function.

studies.title: Betaine improves hyperoxic lung injury through downregulating pulmonary macrophage pyroptosis in newborn mice.
studies.abstract:
Background

Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is a common chronic respiratory disease in preterm infants. NLRP3-mediated macrophage pyroptosis plays a crucial role in the pathogenesis of BPD. Recent evidence suggests that betaine has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant functions. This study aimed to investigate the effect of betaine on pulmonary macrophage pyroptosis in BPD.

Methods

Newborn mice were exposed to either hyperoxia (90%) or room air shortly after birth and treated subcutaneously with betaine daily for 14 days. Lung development, the expression of macrophage pyrolysis-associated proteins and the phospho-forkhead box O1 (p-FOXO1) were evaluated. In vitro, the effect of betaine on the expression of p-FOXO1 was assessed in RAW264.7 macrophages exposed to either 90% oxygen or 21% oxygen, with okadaic acid (OA) as phosphatase inhibitor.

Results

Hyperoxia induced macrophage pyroptosis and impaired lung development in newborn mice. Betaine inhibited p-FOXO1 expression and NLRP3-mediated pyroptosis in pulmonary and promoted lung development in the hyperoxia-exposed mice. In vitro, betaine suppressed FOXO1 phosphorylation and NLRP3-mediated pyroptosis under 90% oxygen in RAW264.7 cells, and OA administration reversed these effects.

Conclusion

Betaine may reduce the expression of inflammatory cytokines, downregulate macrophage pyroptosis by inhibiting the phosphorylation of FOXO1, and improve lung development in BPD.

Impact

Our previous research showed that plasma betaine levels at 36 weeks postmenstrual age (PMA) were significantly lower in preterm infants with BPD compared to those without BPD. Betaine has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant functions. However, its role in pulmonary macrophage pyroptosis in BPD remains unknown. The study shows that betaine may downregulate macrophage pyroptosis by inhibiting FOXO1 phosphorylation, alleviate lung inflammation, and improve lung development in BPD.

studies.title: Dietary betaine for fattening Californian rabbits: in vivo and in silico insights into growth, blood physiology, and nutrient utilization.
studies.abstract: To find safe alternatives to antibiotics in rabbit feeds, this study examined the effects of dietary supplementation betaine (trimethylglycine) on fattening Californian rabbits. Seventy-two male Californian rabbits, weaned at 5 weeks of age, were randomly allocated to three dietary treatment groups (n = 24 per group) using a completely randomized design. The experimental diets included a basal diet supplemented with betaine (BET) at 0, 1, or 1.5 g/kg (BET0, BET1, and BET1.5, respectively). The effects of these BET levels were assessed on growth performance, blood hematology, metabolic profile, carcass traits, nutrient digestibility, and feeding values as well as molecular docking analysis. The results showed that dietary BET significantly improved live body weight (LBW) and weight gain at 13 weeks (P < 0.01), while feed intake was reduced (P < 0.05). A significant improvement in the feed conversion ratio (FCR) was also observed, as indicated by lower FCR values (P < 0.05). BET supplementation did not alter carcass traits significantly (P > 0.05). Dietary BET supplementation significantly improved red blood cells (RBCs) count (P < 0.01), hemoglobin (Hg) concentration (P < 0.01), platelet count (P < 0.05), and hematocrit (Ht) levels (P < 0.01) in a dose-dependent manner. Conversely, the white blood cells (WBCs) count was significantly reduced (P < 0.01) in response to BET addition. Rabbits fed a diet supplemented with BET exhibited higher albumin levels and lower aspartate aminotransferase (AST) values (P < 0.01) compared to those fed a BET-free diet. Dietary BET supplementation significantly improved the digestibility coefficients of organic matter (OM), crude protein (CP), crude fiber (CF), and nitrogen-free extract (NFE) (P < 0.05), as well as the feeding values of digestible crude protein (DCP), total digestible nutrients (TDN), and metabolizable energy (ME) (P < 0.05). Molecular docking analysis shed light on BET’s mechanism, revealing its strong binding affinity to proteins involved in antioxidant and apoptosis/inflammatory signaling pathways in growing rabbits. The calculated binding energies confirmed this interaction, showing affinities of -3.58 kcal/mol for cyclooxygenase-2, -3.33 kcal/mol for SOD, -3.23 kcal/mol for BAX, and − 2.89 kcal/mol for caspase-3. In summary, supplementing fattening rabbit diets with BET positively impacted growth attributes, feeding values, nutrient digestibility, and blood metabolic pathways. These benefits are attributed to BET’s antioxidant and anti-apoptotic/anti-inflammatory activities. Our findings suggest that BET has significant potential as a safe and effective alternative to antibiotic growth promoters in rabbit farming, fostering a more sustainable and environmentally conscious industry.

studies.title: Betaine attenuates fatty changes via antioxidant responses against oxytetracycline-induced fatty liver in rats.
studies.abstract:
Aim

This study aimed to investigate the antioxidant properties of betaine against oxytetracycline-induced fatty liver disease.

Background

During the past decades, fatty liver has been considered a public health concern, with prevalence between 10-24% in the world. Betaine has been shown to have some antioxidant properties in our previous studies.

Methods

For this purpose, 32 male Wistar rats, were divided into four groups: control, betaine (Bet., betaine 10 mg/kg daily for 15 days, orally), fatty liver (Fat., induction of fatty liver with oxytetracycline 120 mg/kg during three consecutive days, ip), and fatty liver + betaine group (Fat. + Bet.). On the 19th day, after complete anesthesia, blood samples were taken from the heart, and the liver was sampled for biochemical and histopathology evaluations.

Results

Betaine significantly increased glutathione peroxidase activity (Gpx) in the Bet. and Fat. + Bet. Groups compared to the Fat group (P <0.05). In this regard, glutathione (GSH) content and the total antioxidant capacity (TAC) increased significantly in the betaine-treated rats and Fat. + Bet. group compared to the Fat. Group (P <0.05). Regarding lipid peroxidation, malondialdehyde concentration significantly decreased in Bet. and Fat. + Bet. Groups, when compared to fat. Group (P <0.05). Betaine was able to reduce tissue necrosis and decrease the number of Kupffer cells, restoring the standard color of the cytoplasm of hepatocytes.

Conclusion

The antioxidant properties of betaine are able to prevent fatty liver and oxidative stress in the oxytetracycline-induced fatty liver of rats. The antioxidant properties of betaine appear to prevent fatty liver and oxidative stress in rats with oxytetracycline-induced fatty liver.
studies.journal: Gastroenterology and hepatology from bed to bench

studies.title: Ameliorative effects of betaine on cisplatin-induced cardiotoxicity in rats through anti-inflammatory pathways.
studies.abstract: Cisplatin (CS) is a broad-spectrum chemotherapeutic agent that causes serious adverse effects, such as cardiotoxicity, despite its potent anti-tumor efficacy. This study aimed to evaluate the cardioprotective effects of betaine in rats exposed to repeated low-dose CS administration using histopathological and immunohistochemical methods. Forty female Wistar albino rats were divided into four groups, including control, betaine, CS, and CS + betaine. Betaine (250 mg kg<sup>-1</sup>) was administered orally on a daily basis for four weeks, while CS (8.00 mg kg<sup>-1</sup>) was administered intraperitoneally once a week for the same duration. Cardiomyocytes were then examined using histopathological and immunohistochemical methods. The data were analyzed using one-way analysis of variance and Tukey tests. Histopathological analysis revealed cardiomyocyte disorganization, myofibril loss, and increased eosinophilia in the CS group. Betaine treatment partially prevented CS-induced histological damage, contributing to the cardiac muscle structure preservation. Immunohistochemical analyses demonstrated a significant increase in transforming growth factor-beta and interferon gamma expressions in the CS group, whereas betaine administration reduced transforming growth factor-beta levels. Interleukin 6 expression was lower in the CS + betaine group compared to the CS group. No significant differences were observed between groups regarding Interleukin-1β expression. These findings suggest that betaine may have protective effects against CS-induced cardiotoxicity. Its anti-inflammatory properties appear to mitigate cardiomyocyte damage.
studies.journal: Veterinary research forum : an international quarterly journal

studies.title: Dietary betaine supplementation improved egg quality and gut microbes of laying hens under dexamethasone-induced oxidative stress.
studies.abstract: Oxidative stress is a frequent concern in the breeding of laying hens, and limit the healthy development of poultry. Dexamethasone (DXM) has been demonstrated to induce oxidative stress. Conversely, betaine is an alkaloid with a potent antioxidant activity. The study was designed to investigate the ameliorative effect of betaine on DXM-induced oxidative stress in laying hens. The results revealed that DXM treatment significantly decreased laying rate, shell strength, albumen height, Haugh unit, egg weight, folk weight and albumen weight, alongside increased malondialdehyde (MDA) and decreased total antioxidant capacity (T-AOC) in serum and liver (P < 0.05). In contrast, dietary betaine addition reversed those parameters mentioned above (P < 0.05). Hepatic RNA-seq analysis showed that there existed 110 up- and 88 down-regulated genes in DXM group when compared with the control. Meanwhile there were 117 upregulation and 169 downregulation genes in BT group when compared with DXM group. Besides, we found that dietary betaine addition significantly down-regulated cell adhesion molecules, glycerolipid metabolism and glycolysis gluconeogenesis pathways. In addition, a total of 44 and 94 differential metabolites were identified respectively from Con vs. DXM and DXM vs BT. More importantly, dietary betaine addition significantly increased the levels of pantothenic acid, gamma-Aminobutyric acid, equol and choline, all of which were related to antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. Furthermore, gut microbiota analysis indicated that the Chao and Observed_species indexes were remarkably higher in BT group (P<0.05). Heatmap analysis revealed that Subdoligranulum, Prevotella, Blautia, YRC22, Bacteroides, Ruminococcus and Coprococcus were notably restored in BT group (P<0.05). Taken together, our findings collectively illustrate that dietary betaine addition could attenuate DXM-induced oxidative stress, improve egg quality and gut microbes of laying hens.

studies.title: Betaine and feed restriction as potential mitigation strategies against heat stress in two strains of laying hens.
studies.abstract: Climate change is increasingly manifesting in temperate regions. Laying hens are highly sensitive to heat stress and mitigation strategies should be implemented to reduce the negative effects. The goal of this experiment was to evaluate the effects of betaine in drinking water (0.55 g/L) and 4 h feed restriction during peak heat stress on laying performance, egg quality, blood gas parameters, body temperature (Tb), and oxidative stress in 2 different breeds of laying hens. Therefore, 448 ISA Brown hens (25 wk) and 448 Lohmann LSL classic laying hens (26 wk) were housed in 128 cages (7 hens/cage). Thermoneutral (TN) data was collected for 21 d before cyclic heat stress (HS) (21d; 32 ± 2°C; 6 h daily). During HS, hens were divided into 4 treatments: 1) feed restriction (FR), 2) betaine supplementation in drinking water (BET), 3) feed restriction and betaine supplementation in drinking water (FR-BET), or 4) control (CON). The effects were evaluated after 1 wk of HS (acute heat stress; AHS) and 3 wk of HS (chronic heat stress; CHS). Laying rate and egg mass (EM) diminished during CHS but decreased more in white than brown hens (2.78% and 1.94%; -1.57% and -0.81%, respectively; P = 0.004) and remained unaltered by BET or FR. During AHS, average daily feed intake (ADFI) increased compared to TN, but the increase was higher in white than brown hens (6.36% and 2.62%, respectively; P = 0.001). studies.title: Betaine supplementation alleviates dextran sulfate sodium-induced colitis
studies.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a multifaceted and recurrent immune disorder that occurs in the gastrointestinal tract. Betaine is a natural compound that exerts beneficial anti-inflammatory effects. However, the role of betaine in protecting IBD is still unclear. Therefore, the aim of our study was to investigate the anti-inflammatory effect of betaine in dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis. The results showed that betaine greatly increased the body weight and decreased the disease activity index score of DSS-treated mice. Furthermore, betaine effectively downregulated the protein levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, and TNFα) and upregulated tight junction proteins (occludin and ZO-1) in the mice. Additionally, betaine exposure remarkably restricted the DSS-induced phosphorylation of IκB and NF-κB p65 in mice. Similarly, betaine pretreatment improved the inflammatory response and intestinal barrier of Caco-2 cells. Betaine altered the gut microbiota composition, markedly decreasing the relative abundance of Firmicutes and Proteobacteria and considerably increasing the relative abundance of Bacteroidota and Campylobacterota in DSS-induced mice. In conclusion, betaine could attenuate colitis

studies.title: Effects of dietary betaine supplementation on biochemical parameters of blood and testicular oxidative stress in Hu sheep.
studies.abstract: Betaine, a highly valuable feed additive, has been observed to alter the distribution of protein and fat in the bodies of ruminants and to exhibit strong antioxidant properties. However, the effects of dietary betaine supplementation on the biochemical parameters of blood and on testicular oxidative stress remain unknown. This study aimed to investigate the effects of dietary betaine supplementation on lipid metabolism, immunity, and testicular oxidative status in Hu sheep. Experimental sheep (n=3, three sheep per group) were fed betaine-containing diets, a basal diet supplemented with 0 g/day (control group), 1 g/day (B1), and 3 g/day betaine (B2). There were no differences in the serum concentrations of triglycerides and cholesterol in Hu sheep receiving diets supplemented with betaine. The ratio of basophils significantly increased in the B1 and B2 groups. ELISA (enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay) results showed that testicular superoxide dismutase (SOD) and glutathione peroxidase (GSH-Px) activity were significantly higher, whereas malondialdehyde (MDA) content significantly decreased, after feeding betaine-supplemented diets. qPCR results showed that the mRNA expression levels of CAT, SOD2, and GSH-Px were significantly upregulated in both the B1 and B2 groups compared to those in the control group. Furthermore, the expression of proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) was significantly lower in the testes of betaine-treated Hu sheep than in the control group. Moreover, LKB1 (liver kinase B1) expression significantly increased, and mRNA expression of AMPK (AMP-activated serine/threonine protein kinase) significantly decreased in the B1 group. The relative gene expression of mTOR (mechanistic target of rapamycin) was significantly higher in the B2 group than in the control group. RAPTOR expression significantly increased in the B1 group. Western blot revealed that the ratio of P-mTOR and mTOR significantly increased after feeding betaine-supplemented diets. In conclusion, betaine supplementation improved serum lipid metabolism, immune response, and increased the testicular antioxidant capacity of Hu sheep, which might be regulated via mTOR signaling pathway.

studies.title: Effect of Betaine Supplementation on Liver Tissue and Ultrastructural Changes in Methionine-Choline-Deficient Diet-Induced NAFLD.
studies.abstract: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) represents a hepatic manifestation of metabolic syndrome. The aim of this study was to examine the effect of betaine on ultrastructural changes in the mouse liver with methionine- and choline-deficient (MCD) diet-induced NAFLD. Male C57BL/6 mice were divided into groups: Control-fed with standard chow, BET-standard chow supplemented with betaine (1.5% w/v drinking water), MCD-fed with MCD diet, and MCD + BET-MCD diet with betaine supplementation for 6 weeks. Liver samples were taken for pathohistology and transmission electron microscopy. The MCD diet-induced steatosis, inflammation, and balloon-altered hepatocytes were alleviated by betaine. MCD diet induced an increase in mitochondrial size versus the control group (p < 0.01), which was decreased in the betaine-treated group. In the MCD diet-fed group, the total mitochondrial count decreased versus the control group (p < 0.01), while it increased in the MCD + BET group versus MCD (p < 0.01). Electron microscopy showed an increase in the number of autophagosomes in the MCD and MCD + BET group versus control, and a significant difference in autophagosomes number was detected in the MCD + BET group by comparison with the MCD diet-treated group (p < 0.05). Betaine decreases the number of enlarged mitochondria, alleviates steatosis, and increases the number of autophagosomes in the liver of mice with NAFLD.

studies.title: Betaine Supplementation Enhances Lipid Metabolism and Improves Insulin Resistance in Mice Fed a High-Fat Diet.
studies.abstract: Obesity is a major driver of metabolic diseases such as nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, certain cancers, and insulin resistance. However, there are no effective drugs to treat obesity. Betaine is a nontoxic, chemically stable and naturally occurring molecule. This study shows that dietary betaine supplementation significantly inhibits the white fat production in a high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obese mice. This might be due to betaine preventing the formation of new white fat (WAT), and guiding the original WAT to burn through stimulated mitochondrial biogenesis and promoting browning of WAT. Furthermore, dietary betaine supplementation decreases intramyocellular lipid accumulation in HFD-induced obese mice. Further analysis shows that betaine supplementation reduced intramyocellular lipid accumulation might be associated with increasing polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA), fatty acid oxidation, and the inhibition of fatty acid synthesis in muscle. Notably, by performing insulin-tolerance tests (ITTs) and glucose-tolerance tests (GTTs), dietary betaine supplementation could be observed for improvement of obesity and non-obesity induced insulin resistance. Together, these findings could suggest that inhibiting WAT production, intramyocellular lipid accumulation and inflammation, betaine supplementation limits HFD-induced obesity and improves insulin resistance.

studies.title: Effects of betaine supplementation on nitric oxide metabolism, atherosclerotic parameters, and fatty liver in guinea pigs fed a high cholesterol plus methionine
studies.abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of high cholesterol (CHOL) and CHOL + methionine (MET) diets on atherogenic and oxidative index parameters and on the factors that influence nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability. Also, attempts were made to determine whether dietary betaine (BET) resulted in any improvement in the changes that occurred after CHOL + MET administration. Guinea pigs were fed chow containing 1.5% CHOL with or without 2% MET for 10 wk. A third group received the CHOL + MET + BET diet. Control groups were given standard chow or standard chow + BET. Arginine, NO, nitrotyrosine (NT), and asymmetric dimethylarginine (ADMA) levels; lipid profile; and dimethylarginine dimethylaminohydrolase (DDAH) activity were measured. The liver and aorta were subjected to histopathologic analysis. The CHOL + MET diet caused higher serum CHOL and homocysteine levels, but no further increases were seen in aortic CHOL and diene conjugate (DC) levels and histopathologic lesions as compared with the CHOL group. Hepatic lipids and DC levels were also higher, and histopathologic lesions were more severe. CHOL + MET feeding increased ADMA and NT levels as compared with those of the CHOL-fed group. When BET (1 g/kg body weight/d) was added to the CHOL + MET diet, homocysteine and lipid levels decreased and histopathologic changes were reversed. BET diet decreased serum ADMA and hepatic and aortic DC levels and partly restored DDAH activity. BET supplementation may be effective in preventing hyperlipidemia, disturbed NO availability, oxidative stress, and the development of fatty liver and atherosclerotic lesions that might result from excess amounts of cholesterol and methionine in the diet.

studies.title: High-Fat Diet, Betaine, and Polydextrose Induce Changes in Adipose Tissue Inflammation and Metabolism in C57BL/6J Mice.
studies.abstract: High-fat diets are a likely cause of low-grade inflammation and obesity-related pathologies. This study measures the effects of a high-fat diet, in combination with two dietary supplements-betaine and polydextrose-on metabolism and inflammation in the adipose tissue of diet-induced obese mice. Forty male C57BL/6J mice are fed a high-fat diet for 8 weeks and compared with low-fat-diet-fed control animals (n = 10). For the last 4 weeks, the high-fat-diet-fed animals are supplemented with 1% betaine, 3.33% polydextrose, their combination, or plain water. Fat depots from subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue are analyzed for inflammatory markers and nontargeted metabolomics by quantitative PCR and LC-QTOF-MS. The high-fat diet significantly increases adipose tissue inflammation in both fat depots. By metabolic profiling, clear differences are noted between low-fat-diet and high-fat-diet groups with regard to the levels of several metabolite species-primarily carnitines, lipids, and amino acids. Dietary betaine mitigates the high-fat-diet-induced IL-6 expression and significantly increases betaine and butyrobetaine levels in adipose tissue. The high-fat diet induces patent changes in carnitine and lipid metabolism in adipose tissue. Betaine supplementation elevates the levels of betaine and its derivatives and certain carnitine species, as reported in muscle and liver, and moderately reduces inflammation.

studies.title: Attenuation of heat stress-induced spermatogenesis complications by betaine in mice.
studies.abstract: High temperatures can induce oxidative stress, impairment of spermatogenesis, and reduction of sperm quality and quantity concomitant with transient periods of partial or complete infertility in male mammals. Promising beneficial effects of betaine supplementation on the epididymal spermatozoa have been reported in experimental studies; however, its effects on testicular heat stress (HS)-induced impairment have yet to be determined. In the present study, betaine (Bet) was orally administrated (250 mg/kg day) during a 14-day period, before (Bet + HS group) or after (HS + Bet group) induction of testicular HS in 7-9 week-old male mice. HS was induced by testicular immersion in water at 42 °C in stress groups. Epididymal spermatozoa and testes were collected at days 14 and 28 after HS induction in order to analyze sperm characteristics, testicular oxidative status, and histological changes. Our studies showed that HS reduced testicular weight, the quality and quantity of epididymal spermatozoa, and impaired maturation of germinal cells. The levels of MDA, catalase, SOD, and GPX were increased in the testes of HS-induced mice (P < 0.01). Although betaine treatment before and after exposure to HS enhanced antioxidant defense (P < 0.05) and accelerated germinal epithelium regeneration, its effects on the characteristics of epididymal spermatozoa were scarce. On the other hand, in the absence of heat stress, quality and quantity of epididymal spermatozoa were improved following 14 days of betaine consumption. Our study revealed the beneficial effect of betaine on HS-induced complications of spermatogenesis, as well as its potency to improve epididymal spermatozoa in intact mice.

studies.title: Short-Term Impact of Betaine Supplementation on Ruminal Microbial Relative Abundance, Nutrient Digestibility, Serum Metabolites, and Milk Composition in Heat-St
studies.abstract: This short-term study evaluated the effects of dietary betaine supplementation over 4 weeks on feed intake, milk production, nutrient digestibility, blood metabolites, and ruminal microbial communities in heat-stressed Holstein cows. Thirty lactating cows were randomly divided into a control group and a treatment group supplemented with 80 g/day of natural betaine extract for 4 weeks during summer. Betaine supplementation significantly increased dry matter intake (21.0 vs. 18.7 kg/day; p ≤ 0.05) and milk yield (35.4 vs. 31.2 kg/day; p ≤ 0.05) compared to the control. Milk composition, including fat and protein content, also improved (p ≤ 0.05). Cows receiving betaine had lower rectal temperatures (p = 0.02) and respiration rates (p = 0.01), indicating reduced heat stress. Serum concentrations of inflammatory markers-ceruloplasmin, haptoglobin, and serum amyloid A-were significantly lower in the betaine group by Week 4 (p ≤ 0.05). Plasma and rumen amino acid profiles, particularly lysine and methionine, were better preserved in the betaine group (p ≤ 0.05). Ruminal concentrations of volatile fatty acids increased (p ≤ 0.05), and the abundance of beneficial microbial species, such as Fibrobacter succinogenes, Butyrivibrio proteoclasticus, and Megasphaera elsdenii, was enhanced (p ≤ 0.05). These findings suggest that betaine supplementation is an effective nutritional strategy to improve dairy cow performance, reduce inflammation, and stabilise ruminal microbiota during heat stress.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A naturally occurring molecule in cells that supports energy production and cell signaling.
explanation.what_it_is: Betaine (also called glycine betaine or trimethylglycine) is a small organic compound found naturally in cells and foods like beets, spinach, and seafood. Chemically, it is a derivative of the amino acid glycine, with three methyl groups (tiny carbon-hydrogen clusters) attached. People typically take it as a supplement in powder or capsule form, and it's also consumed through diet. It plays roles in cell energy metabolism and in regulating water balance inside cells.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Helps cells produce energy and manages cell water balance; may reduce fatigue and inflammatory markers.
explanation.how_it_works: Betaine works through two main pathways. First, it donates methyl groups (chemical tags that cells use to turn genes on and off and to make other important molecules) in a process called one-carbon metabolism — this helps cells build proteins and produce energy more efficiently. Second, it acts as an osmolyte, meaning it helps cells retain water and maintain their internal salt balance, which is especially important during exercise when cells are stressed and losing fluids. In animal studies, betaine has also been shown to reduce inflammatory markers (immune signals that indicate tissue irritation), though the human evidence for this is limited. How directly these mechanisms translate to the endurance and strength gains observed in human trials is not fully clear, but the consistency of findings suggests betaine does influence physical performance in measurable ways.
explanation.safety_line: Short-term trials reported few side effects; long-term safety and effects in specific populations untested.
explanation.safety_detail: The human trials retrieved reported good tolerability — few adverse events were noted in studies lasting weeks to a few months. However, most trials were relatively short (2–12 weeks) and enrolled healthy or athletic adults, so tolerability in children, pregnant women, people with kidney disease, or those taking multiple medications has not been adequately studied. One study in prediabetes noted no serious safety concerns, but the overall safety database remains narrow.
safety_bullets: Kidney disease: betaine metabolism depends partly on kidney function; untested in renal impairment — consult a doctor if you have kidney disease.
Pregnancy and lactation: no human trials retrieved; unknown safety — avoid without medical guidance.
Drug interactions: no specific interactions retrieved, but betaine affects one-carbon metabolism pathways; may interact with folate, B12, or certain medications — inform your doctor of use.
Long-term use: trials retrieved were 2–12 weeks; safety beyond a few months is understudied.
explanation.chem_meaning: Betaine is a small, water-loving molecule (XLogP 0.5, meaning it dissolves easily in water and in body fluids). This makes it readily absorbed from food and supplements and allows it to move freely through cells and bloodstream. Its small size and hydrophilic nature mean it can cross cell membranes and interact with many metabolic pathways without needing special transporters, which is why it has broad effects on cell energy and osmotic balance.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Across 16 human trials and 37 animal studies (53 total), betaine supplementation improved endurance and exercise performance with a small-to-moderate effect size (standardized mean difference 0.36 [95% CI 0.03 to 0.69]). Recent studies include a 2024 systematic review of 317 participants showing chronic betaine enhanced performance, a 2025 RCT in cyclists demonstrating improved 60 km time trial performance and one-carbon metabolism, and several 2023 RCTs reporting gains in anaerobic power and CrossFit performance. Three independent meta-analyses converge on this finding, suggesting replication across different study groups.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Multiple large systematic reviews in recent years (2024–2025) with consistent human evidence and a pooled effect that excludes zero, plus replication across independent analyses. Over 3200 verified participants across the retrieved trials.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Five human studies and 17 animal studies (22 total) examined betaine's effects on blood lipids. A 2021 meta-analysis found betaine *moderately increased* total cholesterol levels — an effect that is counterintuitive and warrants caution. A 2022 meta-analysis examined broader cardiovascular markers. A 2018 RCT of 27 people with prediabetes found metabolic effects but with mixed lipid results. Total verified participants across human studies: ~1093.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Only 1 primary RCT and 2 pooled analyses in humans (below Strong threshold); human evidence is limited and shows an unexpected direction (cholesterol increase rather than improvement), suggesting the effect is modest and context-dependent.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Eight human trials and 3 animal studies (11 total) assessed strength outcomes, with a pooled effect of 0.47 [95% CI 0.04 to 0.89], suggesting a small-to-moderate improvement. A 2025 narrative review surveyed betaine and aging, finding mixed strength results. A 2024 systematic review of 317 participants noted chronic betaine improved strength markers. A 2023 RCT reported increased strength in CrossFit athletes. However, a 2020 RCT of 15 participants found *no* improvement in muscle hypertrophy or strength over 6 weeks, and a 2021 RCT of soccer players also showed inconsistency. Verified participants: ~391 across 4 of 11 studies.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Four primary human studies and 3 pooled analyses (below Strong); effect size is positive but confidence intervals are wide, and individual trials show conflicting results. Evidence suggests a modest benefit in some contexts (longer durations, high-intensity training) but not universal.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Four human studies and 23 animal studies (27 total) examined inflammatory markers. A 2023 meta-analysis of 277 participants found betaine reduced inflammatory markers in human trials. A 2025 narrative review on betaine and aging reviewed inflammatory evidence. A 2021 RCT in soccer players (n=15) and a 2014 clinical trial in short bowel syndrome also reported anti-inflammatory effects. Animal studies consistently showed reduced inflammatory markers (e.g., TLR4/NF-κB pathway downregulation). Verified human participants: ~578 across 7 of 27 studies.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Only 2 primary human studies and 2 pooled analyses retrieved (below Strong); human evidence is sparse. Animal data is robust, but translation to human clinical anti-inflammatory benefit is not yet confirmed.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence is dominated by 16 human trials for endurance (the strongest outcome) and smaller numbers for strength, lipids, and inflammation (4–8 human trials each). Most studies are RCTs lasting 2–12 weeks and enrolled healthy or athletic adults; very few included older adults, women specifically, or people with chronic diseases. The field has seen recent activity (2023–2026), with three independent meta-analyses converging on endurance benefits. However, for lipids and inflammation, human evidence relies on fewer trials and pooled analyses, limiting confidence.
explanation.open_questions: The retrieved records show that most endurance studies are in athletes or young healthy people; whether betaine benefits sedentary or older adults is unclear. For strength, the records show conflicting individual trials (some positive, some null) despite a positive pooled effect, suggesting the benefit may depend on training type, duration, or dose — but the abstracts provided do not isolate these moderators. For lipids, the unexpected finding (cholesterol increase) is striking but rests on limited human trials, and no mechanistic explanation is visible in the records. For inflammation, the records include mostly animal studies; only a handful of human trials were retrieved, so the evidence in people remains preliminary. Sample sizes are often omitted from abstracts, so true total participant numbers are likely larger than reported but cannot be verified from the data provided.

appraisal.headline: The endurance outcome is reasonably well-supported by convergent meta-analyses, but the other three outcomes rest on very sparse human evidence (1–4 primary trials each), making it unsafe to generalize the 'Strong' tier rating across the compound's claimed benefits.

concerns.issue: Extreme sparsity of human trials for 3 of 4 outcomes
concerns.detail: Cholesterol/lipids, muscle strength, and inflammation each report only 1–4 primary human RCTs in the retrieved records, despite claims of 'Moderate' grades. For cholesterol, only 1 RCT (n=27, 2018) is listed; for inflammation, only 1 RCT (n=15, 2021) and 1 clinical trial (2014). This is below any reasonable threshold for robust inference. A single negative or positive trial can flip the direction of evidence when the base is this thin.

concerns.issue: Massive underreporting of sample sizes across the retrieved evidence
concerns.detail: For endurance (53 studies), only 15 report n; for cholesterol (22 studies), only 8; for strength (11 studies), only 4; for inflammation (27 studies), only 7. The engine explicitly notes 'most abstracts omit sample size, so the true total is substantially larger.' This means the precision claims are inferred, not observed—and concealed small-sample studies could be over-weighting the pooled estimates. The true composition of the evidence base is opaque.

concerns.issue: Dominance of animal and unclassified studies in non-endurance outcomes
concerns.detail: For cholesterol: 16/22 are animal studies; for inflammation: 22/27 are animal; for strength: 3/11 are animal. Animal models do not reliably predict human metabolism or lipid/inflammatory responses. The human evidence for these outcomes is not just small—it is vastly outnumbered by preclinical work that may not translate. The 'Moderate' grades appear to rely on animal data to pad the sample.

concerns.issue: Inconsistency within endurance outcome not fully resolved
concerns.detail: The pooled SMD for endurance is 0.36 [0.03 to 0.69], with the confidence interval including near-zero effect. Although 3 meta-analyses are cited as converging, individual trial results in the records show heterogeneity: a 2020 RCT found betaine 'Does Not Improve Muscle Hypertrophy or Strength Following 6 Weeks,' and a 2012 RCT found 'Creatine but not betaine supplementation increases muscle phosphorylcreatine content and strength.' The pooled estimate masks conflicting findings.

concerns.issue: Absence of extractable pooled effect for cholesterol and inflammation
concerns.detail: Both outcomes report 'pooled effect: none extractable' in the engine notes, yet are graded 'Moderate' rather than 'Insufficient.' This suggests the grades rely on narrative synthesis or indirect inference (e.g., mechanistic plausibility or animal analogs) rather than quantitative meta-analysis. Without a pooled estimate, it is unclear what direction or magnitude of effect the grade is endorsing.

appraisal.mechanism_check: Betaine's role in one-carbon metabolism and homocysteine reduction is biochemically sound; however, the leap from homocysteine lowering to improved endurance performance or reduced cholesterol in humans is incompletely validated in the retrieved evidence. The 2025 cycling trial explicitly measured 'one-carbon metabolism,' suggesting investigators are testing the mechanism, but the retrieved records do not show whether improved one-carbon flux actually correlates with the claimed clinical outcomes. For inflammation and strength, the mechanistic link is even more tenuous—animal studies may show betaine reduces inflammatory markers or supports protein synthesis, but human evidence of these pathways in the retrieved trials is minimal.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would argue that the endurance grade rests on a pooled effect (SMD 0.36) with a confidence interval touching zero and on heterogeneous primary trials, some of which found no benefit. For the other outcomes, only 1–4 human trials exist per outcome, and three outcomes lack extractable pooled effects entirely. The 'Strong' rating at the compound level appears inflated by the endurance outcome; grading endurance as 'Strong' while cholesterol, strength, and inflammation are 'Moderate' would be more defensible. The current tier conflates strong evidence for one outcome with moderate/insufficient evidence for others, misleading readers into believing betaine is robustly supported across multiple domains.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: For cholesterol and inflammation: well-powered RCTs (n ≥ 100) with pre-registered endpoints and biomarker validation would establish whether the animal and small-trial signals translate to humans. For endurance: larger trials (n ≥ 300) across diverse populations (not just athletes) with standardized protocols would clarify whether the 0.36 SMD is a robust effect or a scatter-plot artifact. For all outcomes: transparency on funding sources and registration status would help assess bias risk, which is not visible in these records.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Una molécula que ocurre naturalmente en las células y apoya la producción de energía y la señalización celular.
explanation_es.what_it_is: La betaína (también llamada glicina betaína o trimetiglicina) es un compuesto orgánico pequeño que se encuentra naturalmente en las células y en alimentos como remolachas, espinacas y mariscos. Químicamente, es un derivado del aminoácido glicina, con tres grupos metilo (pequeños grupos de carbono e hidrógeno) unidos. Las personas típicamente la toman como suplemento en forma de polvo o cápsula, y también se consume a través de la dieta. Desempeña funciones en el metabolismo energético celular y en la regulación del balance de agua dentro de las células.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Ayuda a las células a producir energía y gestiona el balance de agua celular; puede reducir la fatiga y los marcadores inflamatorios.
explanation_es.how_it_works: La betaína funciona a través de dos vías principales. Primero, dona grupos metilo (etiquetas químicas que las células utilizan para activar y desactivar genes y para fabricar otras moléculas importantes) en un proceso llamado metabolismo de un carbono — esto ayuda a las células a fabricar proteínas y producir energía más eficientemente. Segundo, actúa como osmolito, lo que significa que ayuda a las células a retener agua y mantener su balance de sal interno, lo cual es especialmente importante durante el ejercicio cuando las células están estresadas y perdiendo fluidos. En estudios en animales, se ha demostrado que la betaína reduce los marcadores inflamatorios (señales inmunológicas que indican irritación tisular), aunque la evidencia en humanos para esto es limitada. No está completamente claro cómo estos mecanismos se traducen directamente en las ganancias de resistencia y fuerza observadas en ensayos humanos, pero la consistencia de los hallazgos sugiere que la betaína sí influye en el desempeño físico de maneras medibles.
explanation_es.safety_line: Los ensayos a corto plazo reportaron pocos efectos secundarios; la seguridad a largo plazo y los efectos en poblaciones específicas no han sido probados.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos humanos recuperados reportaron buena tolerabilidad — se notaron pocos eventos adversos en estudios que duraron semanas a pocos meses. Sin embargo, la mayoría de los ensayos fueron relativamente cortos (2–12 semanas) e incluyeron adultos sanos o atletas, por lo que la tolerabilidad en niños, mujeres embarazadas, personas con enfermedad renal, o aquellos que toman múltiples medicamentos no ha sido adecuadamente estudiada. Un estudio en prediabetes no notó preocupaciones de seguridad serias, pero la base de datos de seguridad general sigue siendo limitada.
safety_bullets: Enfermedad renal: el metabolismo de la betaína depende parcialmente de la función renal; no ha sido probado en insuficiencia renal — consulte a un médico si tiene enfermedad renal.
Embarazo y lactancia: no se recuperaron ensayos humanos; seguridad desconocida — evite sin orientación médica.

Interacciones con medicamentos: no se recuperaron interacciones específicas, pero la betaína afecta las vías del metabolismo de un carbono; puede interactuar con folato, B12, o ciertos medicamentos — informe a su médico sobre su uso.
Uso a largo plazo: los ensayos recuperados duraron 2–12 semanas; la seguridad más allá de unos pocos meses está insuficientemente estudiada.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: La betaína es una molécula pequeña que ama el agua (XLogP 0,5, lo que significa que se disuelve fácilmente en agua y en fluidos corporales). Esto la hace fácilmente absorbible de alimentos y suplementos y permite que se mueva libremente a través de las células y el torrente sanguíneo. Su tamaño pequeño y naturaleza hidrófila significan que puede atravesar membranas celulares e interactuar con muchas vías metabólicas sin necesitar transportadores especiales, lo cual es por qué tiene efectos amplios en la energía celular y el balance osmótico.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: En 16 ensayos humanos y 37 estudios en animales (53 en total), la suplementación con betaína mejoró la resistencia y el desempeño en el ejercicio con un tamaño de efecto pequeño a moderado (diferencia media estandarizada 0,36 [IC 95% 0,03 a 0,69]). Los estudios recientes incluyen una revisión sistemática 2024 de 317 participantes mostrando que la betaína crónica mejoró el desempeño, un ensayo aleatorizado 2025 en ciclistas demostrando desempeño mejorado en contrarreloj de 60 km y metabolismo de un carbono, y varios ensayos aleatorizados 2023 reportando ganancias en potencia anaeróbica y desempeño en CrossFit. Tres metanálisis independientes convergen en este hallazgo, sugiriendo replicación en diferentes grupos de estudio.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Múltiples grandes revisiones sistemáticas en años recientes (2024–2025) con evidencia humana consistente y un efecto agrupado que excluye cero, más replicación en análisis independientes. Más de 3200 participantes verificados en los ensayos recuperados.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Cinco estudios humanos y 17 estudios en animales (22 en total) examinaron los efectos de la betaína en los lípidos sanguíneos. Un metanálisis 2021 encontró que la betaína *aumentó moderadamente* los niveles de colesterol total — un efecto que es contraintuitivo y requiere cautela. Un metanálisis 2022 examinó marcadores cardiovasculares más amplios. Un ensayo aleatorizado 2018 de 27 personas con prediabetes encontró efectos metabólicos pero con resultados de lípidos mixtos. Participantes verificados totales en estudios humanos: ~1093.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Solo 1 ensayo controlado aleatorizado primario y 2 análisis agrupados en humanos (por debajo del umbral Fuerte); la evidencia humana es limitada y muestra una dirección inesperada (aumento de colesterol en lugar de mejora), sugiriendo que el efecto es modesto y dependiente del contexto.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Ocho ensayos humanos y 3 estudios en animales (11 en total) evaluaron resultados de fuerza, con un efecto agrupado de 0,47 [IC 95% 0,04 a 0,89], sugiriendo una mejora pequeña a moderada. Una revisión narrativa 2025 examinó betaína y envejecimiento, encontrando resultados de fuerza mixtos. Una revisión sistemática 2024 de 317 participantes notó que la betaína crónica mejoró marcadores de fuerza. Un ensayo aleatorizado 2023 reportó aumento de fuerza en atletas de CrossFit. Sin embargo, un ensayo aleatorizado 2020 de 15 participantes encontró *ninguna* mejora en la hipertrofia muscular o la fuerza en 6 semanas, y un ensayo aleatorizado 2021 de jugadores de fútbol también mostró inconsistencia. Participantes verificados: ~391 en 4 de 11 estudios.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Cuatro estudios humanos primarios y 3 análisis agrupados (por debajo de Fuerte); el tamaño del efecto es positivo pero los intervalos de confianza son amplios, y los ensayos individuales muestran resultados conflictivos. La evidencia sugiere un beneficio modesto en algunos contextos (duraciones más largas, entrenamiento de alta intensidad) pero no universal.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Cuatro estudios humanos y 23 estudios en animales (27 en total) examinaron marcadores inflamatorios. Un metanálisis 2023 de 277 participantes encontró que la betaína redujo marcadores inflamatorios en ensayos humanos. Una revisión narrativa 2025 sobre betaína y envejecimiento revisó la evidencia inflamatoria. Un ensayo aleatorizado 2021 en jugadores de fútbol (n=15) y un ensayo clínico 2014 en síndrome de intestino corto también reportaron efectos antiinflamatorios. Los estudios en animales consistentemente mostraron reducción de marcadores inflamatorios (p. ej., regulación a la baja de la vía TLR4/NF-κB). Participantes humanos verificados: ~578 en 7 de 27 estudios.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Solo 2 estudios humanos primarios y 2 análisis agrupados recuperados (por debajo de Fuerte); la evidencia humana es escasa. Los datos en animales son robustos, pero la traducción al beneficio antiinflamatorio clínico humano aún no está confirmada.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La evidencia está dominada por 16 ensayos humanos para resistencia (el resultado más fuerte) y números más pequeños para fuerza, lípidos e inflamación (4–8 ensayos humanos cada uno). La mayoría de los estudios son ensayos aleatorizados durando 2–12 semanas e incluyeron adultos sanos o atletas; muy pocos incluyeron adultos mayores, mujeres específicamente, o personas con enfermedades crónicas. El campo ha visto actividad reciente (2023–2026), con tres metanálisis independientes convergiendo en beneficios de resistencia. Sin embargo, para lípidos e inflamación, la evidencia humana se basa en menos ensayos y análisis agrupados, limitando la confianza.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros recuperados muestran que la mayoría de los estudios de resistencia están en atletas o personas jóvenes sanas; si la betaína beneficia a adultos sedentarios o mayores es poco claro. Para fuerza, los registros muestran ensayos individuales conflictivos (algunos positivos, algunos nulos) a pesar de un efecto agrupado positivo, sugiriendo que el beneficio puede depender del tipo de entrenamiento, duración, o dosis — pero los resúmenes proporcionados no aíslan estos moderadores. Para lípidos, el hallazgo inesperado (aumento de colesterol) es notable pero descansa en ensayos humanos limitados, y ninguna explicación mecanística es visible en los registros. Para inflamación, los registros incluyen principalmente estudios en animales; solo un puñado de ensayos humanos fueron recuperados, por lo que la evidencia en personas sigue siendo preliminar. Los tamaños de muestra frecuentemente se omiten en los resúmenes, por lo que los números totales verdaderos de participantes son probablemente más grandes que los reportados pero no pueden ser verificados a partir de los datos proporcionados.

appraisal_es.headline: El resultado de resistencia está razonablemente bien respaldado por metanálisis convergentes, pero los otros tres resultados descansan en evidencia humana muy escasa (1–4 ensayos primarios cada uno), lo que hace que sea inseguro generalizar la clasificación de nivel 'Fuerte' en los beneficios reivindicados del compuesto.

concerns.issue: Escasez extrema de ensayos humanos para 3 de 4 resultados
concerns.detail: Colesterol/lípidos, fuerza muscular e inflamación reportan solo 1–4 ECA primarios humanos en los registros recuperados, a pesar de las afirmaciones de calificaciones 'Moderadas'. Para colesterol, solo se lista 1 ECA (n=27, 2018); para inflamación, solo 1 ECA (n=15, 2021) y 1 ensayo clínico (2014). Esto está por debajo de cualquier umbral razonable para una inferencia robusta. Un único ensayo negativo o positivo puede invertir la dirección de la evidencia cuando la base es tan delgada.

concerns.issue: Subinforme masivo de tamaños de muestra en toda la evidencia recuperada
concerns.detail: Para resistencia (53 estudios), solo 15 reportan n; para colesterol (22 estudios), solo 8; para fuerza (11 estudios), solo 4; para inflamación (27 estudios), solo 7. El motor explícitamente señala 'la mayoría de los resúmenes omiten el tamaño de la muestra, por lo que el total verdadero es sustancialmente mayor.' Esto significa que las afirmaciones de precisión se infieren, no se observan—y los estudios pequeños ocultados podrían estar sobrepesando las estimaciones agrupadas. La verdadera composición de la base de evidencia es opaca.

concerns.issue: Dominancia de estudios animales y sin clasificar en resultados no endocrinos
concerns.detail: Para colesterol: 16/22 son estudios en animales; para inflamación: 22/27 son animales; para fuerza: 3/11 son animales. Los modelos animales no predicen de manera confiable el metabolismo humano o las respuestas lipídicas/inflamatorias. La evidencia humana para estos resultados no es solo pequeña—está vastamente superada por trabajo preclínico que puede no traducirse. Las calificaciones 'Moderadas' parecen depender de datos animales para rellenar la muestra.

concerns.issue: Inconsistencia dentro del resultado de resistencia no completamente resuelta
concerns.detail: La DME agrupada para resistencia es 0.36 [0.03 a 0.69], con el intervalo de confianza incluyendo efecto casi cero. Aunque se citan 3 metanálisis como convergentes, los resultados de ensayos individuales en los registros muestran heterogeneidad: un ECA de 2020 encontró que la betaína 'No mejora la hipertrofia muscular ni la fuerza después de 6 semanas,' y un ECA de 2012 encontró 'La suplementación de creatina pero no de betaína aumenta el contenido de fosfocreatina muscular y la fuerza.' La estimación agrupada enmascara hallazgos conflictivos.

concerns.issue: Ausencia de efecto agrupado extraíble para colesterol e inflamación
concerns.detail: Ambos resultados reportan 'efecto agrupado: ninguno extraíble' en las notas del motor, pero están calificados como 'Moderado' en lugar de 'Insuficiente.' Esto sugiere que las calificaciones dependen de síntesis narrativa o inferencia indirecta (p. ej., plausibilidad mecanística o análogos animales) en lugar de metanálisis cuantitativo. Sin una estimación agrupada, es poco claro qué dirección o magnitud de efecto la calificación está respaldando.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: El papel de la betaína en el metabolismo de un carbono y la reducción de homocisteína es bioquímicamente sólido; sin embargo, el salto de la reducción de homocisteína al rendimiento de resistencia mejorado o colesterol reducido en humanos está incompletamente validado en la evidencia recuperada. El ensayo de ciclismo de 2025 midió explícitamente 'metabolismo de un carbono,' sugiriendo que los investigadores están probando el mecanismo, pero los registros recuperados no muestran si el flujo mejorado de un carbono se correlaciona realmente con los resultados clínicos reivindicados. Para inflamación y fuerza, el vínculo mecanístico es aún más tenue—los estudios en animales pueden mostrar que la betaína reduce marcadores inflamatorios o respalda la síntesis de proteínas, pero la evidencia humana de estas vías en los ensayos recuperados es mínima.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico argumentaría que la calificación de resistencia descansa en un efecto agrupado (DME 0.36) con un intervalo de confianza tocando cero y en ensayos primarios heterogéneos, algunos de los cuales no encontraron beneficio. Para los otros resultados, solo existen 1–4 ensayos humanos por resultado, y tres resultados carecen completamente de efectos agrupados extraíbles. La calificación 'Fuerte' a nivel del compuesto parece inflada por el resultado de resistencia; calificar la resistencia como 'Fuerte' mientras que colesterol, fuerza e inflamación son 'Moderados' sería más defendible. El nivel actual conflate evidencia fuerte para un resultado con evidencia moderada/insuficiente para otros, engañando a los lectores haciéndoles creer que la betaína está sólidamente respaldada en múltiples dominios.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Para colesterol e inflamación: ECA bien potenciados (n ≥ 100) con puntos finales preregistrados y validación de biomarcadores establecerían si las señales animales y de pequeños ensayos se traducen a humanos. Para resistencia: ensayos más grandes (n ≥ 300) en poblaciones diversas (no solo atletas) con protocolos estandarizados aclarían si la DME de 0.36 es un efecto robusto o un artefacto de gráfico de dispersión. Para todos los resultados: transparencia en fuentes de financiamiento y estado de registro ayudaría a evaluar el riesgo de sesgo, que no es visible en estos registros.
